text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read, so other people can understand it quickly. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. For example, choose names like "totalPrice" instead of "tp", so the purpose of each variable is obvious. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused. Each function should do one job well. When code is clean, it is much easier to maintain. You can find and fix bugs faster, and adding new features becomes simpler. In short, clean code saves time and helps teams work together more effectively.
